summary: Larry DeVries is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Minnesota. He held teaching posts at Minnesota, Hawaii, and Washington, a research role at Chicago, and was attested at Langara College in 2005.

Lars Fogelin is an archaeologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse (born 1950) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo (~1975–1997), Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn. He also taught at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, later serving as its abbot (~1976–1984). He was also a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (~1976–1977).

Latika Lahiri (1923–2008) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. An Indian Government scholar, she studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1958–1961) and held a post at the University of Delhi (~1969–1988).

Laura Harrington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, as well as teachers including Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, and Lobsang Jamspal.

Lauran Hartley is a Tibetologist who has served as an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University and a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University. She was also attested at Rutgers University and the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library in 2003.

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) studied medicine at the University of Glasgow (~1873–1878) before working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served in the British Army (~1880–1917), Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata (1896), and University College London (1906–1908).

Laurie L. Patton (born 1961) specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard (~1979–1983) and the University of Chicago (~1984–1991), she held posts at Emory University (~1996–2011), Duke University (~2011–2015), and Middlebury College (~2015).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies. His appointments include serving as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence McCrea specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Cornell University (~1985–1989) and the University of Chicago (~1991–1998) under Sheldon Pollock (~1992–1998), later taking up a post at Cornell University (~2009).

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. His extensive studies include a doctorate from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012), alongside studies at Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, College of Santa Fe, and St. John's College.

Le Manh That (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Saigon (~1962–1965) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1974) before holding a post at Van Hanh University (~1974–1975).

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and completed his studies at Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield (~1899–1903).

Leah Judith Zahler was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson and Geshe Wangyal.

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of anthropology and religious studies. In 2011, he was attested as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University and as a Research Associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan (by 2005) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (1964–1966) under Akira Hirakawa. He held posts at Brown University (1970–1971), Nyingma Institute (1971), and the University of Oriental Studies (attested 1988).

Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen (~1849–1856) and Berlin (~1851–1853) under Benfey, Bopp, and Haupt. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1862–1865) and the Imperial University of Dorpat (~1865–1898).

Leon Hurvitz (1923–1992) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held a professorship at the University of Washington (attested 1965–1973) and served as a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1992).
